source_text: לִ֭/נְצֹר אָרְח֣וֹת מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וְ/דֶ֖רֶךְ חסיד/ו יִשְׁמֹֽר׃
english_snapshot: to guard the paths of justice, and he watches over the way of his faithful ones[a].

signals.text: The Hebrew written text has singular “his faithful one”; the traditional reading has plural “his faithful ones.”

english_snapshot: It will be healing to your navel[a] and refreshment to your bones[b].

signals.text: The Hebrew word is rare and uncertain; it is traditionally understood as “navel,” though some interpret it more broadly as the body.

source_text: שֵֽׂכֶל ט֭וֹב יִתֶּן חֵ֑ן וְ/דֶ֖רֶךְ בֹּגְדִ֣ים אֵיתָֽן־־׃
english_snapshot: Good sense wins favor[a], but the way of the treacherous is hard.[b]

signals.text: The Hebrew word commonly denotes what is enduring, firm, or strong; here it may describe the way as hard or unyielding.

source_text: עֲטֶ֣רֶת חֲכָמִ֣ים עָשְׁרָ֑/ם אִוֶּ֖לֶת כְּסִילִ֣ים אִוֶּֽלֶת׃
english_snapshot: The crown of the wise is their wealth[a], but the folly of fools is folly.

signals.text: Or, following some ancient versions and interpreters, 'the wealth of fools is folly.' The Masoretic Text reads literally, 'the folly of fools is folly.'

source_text: לֵ֣ב נָ֭בוֹן יְבַקֶּשׁ דָּ֑עַת ו/פני כְ֝סִילִ֗ים יִרְעֶ֥ה אִוֶּֽלֶת־׃
english_snapshot: The heart of the discerning seeks knowledge[a], but the face of fools feeds on folly.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'but the face of fools feeds on folly.' The Masoretic Text reads 'face(s) of fools'; many translations render the sense as 'mouth of fools' to fit the parallel image of feeding.

source_text: שֹׁמֵ֣ר מִ֭צְוָה שֹׁמֵ֣ר נַפְשׁ֑/וֹ בּוֹזֵ֖ה דְרָכָ֣י/ו יומת׃
english_snapshot: Whoever keeps the commandment preserves his life[a], but whoever is careless about his ways will die[b].

signals.text: Or “will be put to death” (written consonants); the Masoretic marginal reading is “will die.”

source_text: לְֽקַח בִּ֭גְד/וֹ כִּי עָ֣רַב זָ֑ר וּ/בְעַ֖ד נכרים חַבְלֵֽ/הוּ־־׃
english_snapshot: Take his garment, for he has guaranteed a stranger’s debt; take it as security for a foreign woman.[a]

signals.text: The consonantal text may be read “foreigners,” but the traditional Masoretic reading is singular: “a foreign woman.”

source_text: הֵעֵ֬ז אִ֣ישׁ רָשָׁ֣ע בְּ/פָנָ֑י/ו וְ֝/יָשָׁ֗ר ה֤וּא יכין דרכי/ו׀׃
english_snapshot: A wicked man puts on a bold face[a], but an upright man considers his way.[b]

signals.text: The Masoretic marginal reading is “considers his way.” The written consonantal text can be read, “makes his ways firm.”

source_text: תְּנָֽ/ה בְנִ֣/י לִבְּ/ךָ֣ לִ֑/י וְ֝/עֵינֶ֗י/ךָ דְּרָכַ֥/י תרצנה־׃
english_snapshot: My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes delight in my ways.[a]

signals.text: The written form supports “delight in”; the traditional reading supports “guard” or “keep” my ways.

english_snapshot: lest one who hears it shame you, and your bad reputation never leaves you.[a]

signals.text: The Hebrew is difficult. Literally, the final clause is approximately “and your bad report will not return”; it may mean that the damaging report cannot be withdrawn or that the resulting disgrace does not pass away.

source_text: אָ֘כֹ֤ל דְּבַ֣שׁ הַרְבּ֣וֹת לֹא ט֑וֹב וְ/חֵ֖קֶר כְּבֹדָ֣/ם כָּבֽוֹד־׃
english_snapshot: To eat much honey is not good[a], and to search out their glory is glory.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'and searching out their glory is glory.' The second line is difficult. It may mean that seeking honor for oneself is not honorable, or that investigating weighty matters is honorable. The Masoretic Text is rendered closely here.

source_text: כַּ/צִּפּ֣וֹר לָ֭/נוּד כַּ/דְּר֣וֹר לָ/ע֑וּף כֵּ֥ן קִֽלְלַ֥ת חִ֝נָּ֗ם לא תָבֹֽא׃
english_snapshot: Like a bird in its wandering, like a swallow in its flight, so an undeserved curse does not come.[a]

signals.text: The written Hebrew text reads “does not come”; the traditional reading is “does not come to him.”

source_text: מְפַנֵּ֣ק מִ/נֹּ֣עַר עַבְדּ֑/וֹ וְ֝/אַחֲרִית֗/וֹ יִהְיֶ֥ה מָנֽוֹן׃
english_snapshot: Whoever pampers his slave from youth, in the end he will become like a son.[a]

signals.text: The meaning of the final Hebrew word, מָנוֹן, is uncertain. It has been understood as “a son” or “like a son,” but proposed negative senses include “insolence” and “trouble.”
